questions.q: The SI base unit of luminous intensity is the ______.
questions.e: Luminous intensity is one of the seven SI base quantities and its unit is the candela (cd).

questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the measured value 0.007020?
questions.e: Leading zeros are not significant, but the zero between 2 and the end (trailing zero after the decimal) is, giving 7, 0, 2, 0 = 4 significant figures.

questions.q: Write the dimensional formula of force.
questions.e: Force = mass × acceleration, so its dimensions are [M][LT^-2] = [MLT^-2].

questions.q: The percentage error in measuring the radius of a sphere is 2%. What is the percentage error in its volume?
questions.e: V is proportional to r^3, so the relative error in V is 3 times that in r: 3 × 2% = 6%.

questions.q: The density of water is 1 g/cm^3. Express it in kg/m^3.
The slope of the position-time graph of an object gives its ______.
questions.e: Slope of x-t graph = dx/dt, which is the velocity of the object.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. How far does it travel?
Arjun throws a ball vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, find the maximum height reached.
questions.e: At the top v = 0, so h = u^2/2g = 400/20 = 20 m.

questions.q: The area under the velocity-time graph of a moving object gives its ______.
questions.e: Area under v-t graph = ∫v dt, which equals the displacement in that time interval.

questions.q: A car moving at 72 km/h on the Mumbai–Pune expressway is braked and stops uniformly in 4 s.
p: (a) What is its initial speed in m/s?
(b) What is the magnitude of its deceleration?
(c) What distance does it cover before stopping?
questions.e: 72 km/h = 20 m/s; a = 20/4 = 5 m/s^2; s = average speed × time = 10 × 4 = 40 m.

questions.q: Neglecting air resistance, at what angle of projection is the horizontal range of a projectile maximum?
questions.e: R = u^2 sin2θ/g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

questions.q: A ball is projected at 20 m/s at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. Find its horizontal range (g = 10 m/s^2).
Meera whirls a stone tied to a string in a horizontal circle of radius 0.5 m at a constant speed of 2 m/s. Find its centripetal acceleration.
questions.e: a = v^2/r = 4/0.5 = 8 m/s^2, directed towards the centre.

questions.q: Two vectors of magnitudes 3 units and 4 units act at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
questions.e: For perpendicular vectors, R = √(3^2 + 4^2) = √25 = 5 units.

questions.q: A stone is thrown horizontally at 10 m/s from the top of a cliff 45 m high. How far from the foot of the cliff does it land? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.e: Time of fall t = √(2h/g) = √9 = 3 s; horizontal distance = 10 × 3 = 30 m.

questions.q: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of ______.
questions.e: The first law says a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net force, a property called inertia.

questions.q: What net force is needed to give a 5 kg mass an acceleration of 3 m/s^2?
Impulse of a force is equal to the change in ______ of the body.
questions.e: Impulse = F × Δt = Δp, the change in linear momentum.

questions.q: A cricket ball of mass 0.15 kg moving at 20 m/s is hit straight back by the batsman with the same speed. Find the magnitude of the impulse imparted to the ball.
questions.e: Change in momentum = m(v − u) = 0.15 × (20 − (−20)) = 0.15 × 40 = 6 N s.

questions.q: A 10 kg box rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4 and of kinetic friction is 0.3 (g = 10 m/s^2).
p: (a) What minimum horizontal force will just start the box moving?
(b) What is the kinetic friction force once it is sliding?
(c) If it is pulled with a horizontal force of 50 N, what is its acceleration?
questions.e: Limiting friction = 0.4 × 100 = 40 N; kinetic friction = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N; a = (50 − 30)/10 = 2 m/s^2.

questions.q: The SI unit of power is the ______.
questions.e: Power is work done per unit time; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

questions.q: Find the kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m/s.
The work done by a force acting perpendicular to the displacement is ______.
questions.e: W = Fd cosθ and cos90° = 0, so no work is done (e.g. centripetal force).

questions.q: A motor lifts a 50 kg load through a height of 10 m in 5 s at constant speed. Find the power of the motor (g = 10 m/s^2).
A spring of spring constant 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m. How much potential energy is stored in it?

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: In rotational motion, the quantity that plays the role of mass is called ______.
questions.e: Moment of inertia measures a body's resistance to change in rotational motion, just as mass does for linear motion.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A force of 10 N is applied perpendicular to a spanner at a distance of 0.5 m from the nut. Find the torque.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A spinning dancer pulls her arms inwards and spins faster. This is explained by the conservation of ______.
questions.e: With no external torque, L = Iω is constant; lowering I increases ω.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Find the moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its plane.
questions.e: For a ring, I = MR^2 = 2 × 0.25 = 0.5 kg m^2.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel starts from rest and rotates with a constant angular acceleration of 2 rad/s^2. Its moment of inertia about the axle is 4 kg m^2.
p: (a) What is its angular velocity after 5 s?
(b) Through what angle does it turn in these 5 s?
(c) What torque is acting on it?
questions.e: ω = αt = 10 rad/s; θ = ½αt^2 = 25 rad; τ = Iα = 4 × 2 = 8 N m.

questions.q: The statement that a line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time is Kepler's ______ law.
questions.e: Kepler's second law (law of areas) follows from conservation of angular momentum of the planet.

questions.q: The escape speed from the surface of the Earth is about ______ km/s.
questions.e: v_e = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for the Earth.

questions.q: The value of g on the Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s^2. What is its value at a height equal to the radius of the Earth above the surface?
If the distance between two masses is halved, the gravitational force between them becomes how many times?
questions.e: F is proportional to 1/r^2, so halving r makes F four times larger.

questions.q: A satellite's orbital radius is made 4 times larger. By what factor does its time period increase?
questions.e: By Kepler's third law T^2 ∝ r^3, so T ∝ r^(3/2) = 4^(3/2) = 8.

questions.q: The mode of heat transfer that does not need any material medium is ______.
questions.e: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth through empty space by radiation.

questions.q: Using T(K) = t(°C) + 273, express 27 °C in kelvin.
How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10 °C? (specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg K)
At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same reading?
questions.e: Setting F = C in F = 9C/5 + 32 gives C = −40, so −40 °C = −40 °F.

questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of the law of conservation of ______.
questions.e: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW expresses that energy is conserved when heat and work are exchanged.

questions.q: A thermodynamic process that takes place at constant temperature is called ______.
questions.e: In an isothermal process T stays constant; for an ideal gas, internal energy does not change.

questions.q: A Carnot engine works between a source at 500 K and a sink at 300 K. Find its efficiency.
A gas in a cylinder absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on the surroundings.
p: (a) What is the change in its internal energy?
(b) A process in which no heat enters or leaves the system is called ______.
(c) In such a process, if the gas does 200 J of work, what is the change in internal energy?
questions.e: ΔU = Q − W = 500 − 200 = 300 J; in an adiabatic process Q = 0, so ΔU = −W = −200 J.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the restoring force is directly proportional to the ______ from the mean position.
questions.e: For SHM, F = −kx: the force is proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position.

questions.q: Find the time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m at a place where g = π^2 m/s^2.
A 1 kg block attached to a spring of spring constant 100 N/m oscillates on a smooth surface. Find its angular frequency.
The displacement of a particle in SHM is x = 5 sin(10t) cm, where t is in seconds. What is its maximum speed?
questions.e: v_max = Aω = 5 cm × 10 rad/s = 50 cm/s, reached at the mean position.

questions.q: Sound waves travelling through air are ______ waves.
questions.e: In air, particles vibrate along the direction of propagation, forming compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. Find its speed.
A pipe closed at one end has length 0.85 m. The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s.
p: (b) What is the frequency of the next higher harmonic produced?
(c) Are even harmonics present in a closed pipe? (yes/no)
questions.e: For a closed pipe f1 = v/4L = 340/3.4 = 100 Hz; only odd harmonics (100, 300, 500 Hz ...) are produced.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric charge is the ______.
questions.e: Charge is measured in coulombs; 1 C = 1 A × 1 s.

questions.q: Two point charges of 1 μC each are placed 0.3 m apart in vacuum. Find the force between them (k = 9 × 10^9 N m^2 C^-2).
Electric field lines start from ______ charges and end on negative charges.
questions.e: By convention, field lines originate on positive charges and terminate on negative charges.

questions.q: How many electrons make up a charge of 3.2 × 10^-18 C? (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)
questions.e: By quantisation of charge, n = q/e = 3.2 × 10^-18 / 1.6 × 10^-19 = 20.

questions.q: A charge of 8.85 × 10^-12 C is placed inside a closed cube. Find the total electric flux through the cube (ε0 = 8.85 × 10^-12 C^2 N^-1 m^-2).
questions.e: By Gauss's law, total flux = q/ε0 = 1 N m^2/C, whatever the shape of the closed surface.

questions.q: The SI unit of capacitance is the ______.
questions.e: 1 farad = 1 coulomb per volt.

questions.q: How much work is done in moving a charge of 2 C across a potential difference of 5 V?
Capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance.
A 10 μF capacitor is charged to 100 V. How much energy is stored in it?
A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance of 4 μF with air between the plates.
p: (a) The space is completely filled with a dielectric of K = 5. What is the new capacitance?
(b) It is now connected to a 10 V battery. What charge does it store?
(c) What angle do electric field lines make with equipotential surfaces?
questions.e: C = KC0 = 20 μF; Q = CV = 20 μF × 10 V = 200 μC; field lines are always normal to equipotential surfaces.

questions.q: The SI unit of resistivity is ______.
questions.e: From ρ = RA/l, the unit is Ω × m^2 / m = Ω m.

questions.q: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
questions.e: For n equal resistors in parallel, R = 6/3 = 2 Ω.

questions.q: A wire is stretched uniformly to twice its original length. Its resistance becomes how many times the original?
questions.e: Volume is constant, so doubling l halves A; R = ρl/A becomes 2 × 2 = 4 times.

questions.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 5 Ω. Find the current.
In a metre bridge, an unknown resistance X is in the left gap and 6 Ω in the right gap. The balance point is 40 cm from the left end. Find X.
questions.e: At balance X/6 = 40/60, so X = 4 Ω.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic field is the ______.
questions.e: 1 tesla = 1 N A^-1 m^-1; gauss is a CGS unit.

questions.q: A charge of 2 μC moves at 10^5 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the magnetic force on it.
A galvanometer of resistance 10 Ω gives full-scale deflection for 1 mA. What resistance must be connected in series to convert it into a voltmeter of range 10 V?
A straight wire 2 m long carries 3 A at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the force on it.
A proton enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity perpendicular to the field.
p: (a) What is the shape of its path?
(b) How much work does the magnetic force do on it?
(c) If its speed is doubled, the radius of the path becomes how many times?
questions.e: The force qvB is always perpendicular to v, so it does no work and makes the proton move in a circle of radius r = mv/qB, which is proportional to v.

questions.q: The SI unit of self-inductance is the ______.
questions.e: 1 henry = 1 V s A^-1 = 1 Wb A^-1.

questions.q: The magnetic flux through a single-turn coil falls from 0.5 Wb to 0.1 Wb in 0.2 s. Find the magnitude of the induced emf.
The direction of the induced current is given by ______ law.
questions.e: Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change in flux that produces it, a consequence of energy conservation.

questions.q: A 1 m long metal rod moves at 5 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. Find the motional emf across its ends.
How much energy is stored in an inductor of 2 H carrying a steady current of 3 A?
The frequency of the domestic AC supply in India is ______ Hz.
questions.e: Indian mains supply is 220 V rms at 50 Hz.

questions.q: An ideal step-up transformer has 100 turns in the primary and 500 turns in the secondary. If the input is 220 V, what is the output voltage?
questions.e: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 5, so Vs = 5 × 220 = 1100 V.

questions.q: An inductor of inductance (0.5/π) H is connected to a 50 Hz AC supply. Find its inductive reactance.
Find the resonant angular frequency of an LC circuit with L = 0.1 H and C = 10 μF.
What is the power factor of a purely resistive AC circuit?
questions.e: In a pure resistor, voltage and current are in phase, so φ = 0 and cos φ = 1.

questions.q: Among electromagnetic waves, the ones with the shortest wavelength are ______.
questions.e: Gamma rays, emitted by nuclei, have wavelengths below about 10^-12 m.

questions.q: An FM radio wave has a wavelength of 3 m in vacuum. What is its frequency in MHz? (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
The concept of displacement current was introduced by ______.
questions.e: Maxwell added displacement current to Ampere's law, which led to the prediction of electromagnetic waves.

questions.q: The SI unit of power of a lens is the ______.
questions.e: P = 1/f with f in metres; 1 dioptre = 1 m^-1.

questions.q: Find the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm.
Light travels at 2 × 10^8 m/s in a glass slab. Find the refractive index of the glass (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s).
An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. At what distance from the lens is the image formed?
questions.e: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm (real image on the other side).

questions.q: Find the critical angle for a medium of refractive index 2 with respect to air.
A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 40 cm.
p: (a) What is the power of the convex lens?
(b) What is the power of the combination?
(c) What is the focal length of the combination?

questions.q: Two sources of light that maintain a constant phase difference with each other are called ______ sources.
questions.e: Only coherent sources give a sustained (stationary) interference pattern, which is why both slits in Young's experiment are lit from a single source.

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, λ = 600 nm, slit separation d = 1 mm and screen distance D = 1 m. Find the fringe width in mm.
Light of wavelength 500 nm falls normally on a single slit of width 0.2 mm, and the diffraction pattern is seen on a screen 2 m away. Find the width of the central maximum in mm.
questions.e: Width of central maximum = 2λD/a = 2 × 500 × 10^-9 × 2 / (0.2 × 10^-3) = 0.01 m = 10 mm.

questions.t: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of suitable frequency falls on it is called the ______.
questions.e: Hertz and Lenard observed it; Einstein explained it using photons.

questions.t: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Photons of energy 5 eV fall on a metal of work function 2 eV. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.
questions.e: By Einstein's equation, Kmax = hν − φ0 = 5 − 2 = 3 eV.

questions.t: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through 100 V. Using λ = 1.227/√V nm, find its de Broglie wavelength.

questions.t: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Light of wavelength 620 nm falls on a metal of work function 1.5 eV. Use E(eV) = 1240/λ(nm).
p: (a) What is the energy of each photon?
(b) What is the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons?

questions.q: Doping pure silicon with a pentavalent impurity like phosphorus produces a/an ______-type semiconductor.
questions.e: The fifth valence electron of the donor atom becomes a free electron, so electrons are the majority carriers.

questions.q: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased, the width of its depletion layer ______.
questions.e: The applied voltage opposes the barrier potential, so the depletion region becomes narrower.

questions.q: Ravi builds a centre-tap full-wave rectifier and connects it to the 50 Hz mains through a transformer.
p: (a) A circuit that converts AC into DC is called a ______.
(b) What is the frequency of the ripple in the output?
(c) How many diodes does a centre-tap full-wave rectifier use?
questions.e: Each diode conducts in alternate half-cycles, so the output has two pulses per input cycle, i.e. 2 × 50 = 100 Hz ripple.

questions.q: Pure silicon has intrinsic carrier concentration ni = 1.5 × 10^16 m^-3. It is doped with arsenic so that the electron concentration becomes ne = 4.5 × 10^22 m^-3. Find the hole concentration nh in units of 10^9 m^-3.
The SI unit of stress is ______.
questions.e: Stress = restoring force per unit area, so its SI unit is N/m², i.e. the pascal (Pa).

questions.q: According to Hooke's law, within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to ______.
questions.e: Hooke's law: for small deformations, stress ∝ strain; the constant of proportionality is the modulus of elasticity.

questions.q: The reciprocal of the bulk modulus of a material is called its ______.
questions.e: Compressibility k = 1/B, the fractional change in volume per unit increase in pressure.

questions.q: A wire of length 2 m is stretched so that its length increases by 1 mm. What is the longitudinal strain? Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.e: Strain = ΔL/L = 0.001 m / 2 m = 0.0005 (no unit).

questions.q: A force of 500 N acts normally on a rod of cross-sectional area 2 cm². What is the stress in the rod in pascal?
Substances like rubber and the tissue of the aorta, which can be stretched to cause large strains, are called ______.
questions.e: Such substances have no well-defined plastic region on their stress-strain curve and are called elastomers.

questions.q: A wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 mm² stretches by 1 mm under a load of 100 N. What is the Young's modulus of the material in GPa?
An increase in pressure of 1.0 × 10^7 Pa reduces the volume of a liquid by 0.5%. What is the bulk modulus of the liquid in GPa?
Wire A has length L and radius r; wire B, of the same material, has length 2L and radius 2r. Under the same load, what is the ratio of the extension of A to the extension of B?
questions.e: ΔL = FL/(πr²Y), so ΔL ∝ L/r². A: L/r²; B: 2L/(4r²) = L/(2r²). Ratio A : B = 2.

questions.q: A steel wire is replaced by another steel wire of double the length and double the radius. How does the Young's modulus of the material change?
questions.e: Young's modulus is a property of the material only; it does not depend on the dimensions of the wire, so it stays the same.

questions.q: The equation of continuity, Av = constant, for an incompressible fluid is a consequence of the conservation of ______.
questions.e: The mass of fluid entering a tube of flow per second equals the mass leaving it, giving A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (conservation of mass).

questions.q: The constant maximum velocity finally attained by a body falling through a viscous fluid is called ______ velocity.
questions.e: When viscous force plus buoyancy balances the weight, the net force is zero and the body moves with constant terminal velocity.

questions.q: The SI unit of surface tension is ______.
questions.a: N/m|N m^-1|newton per metre|newton per meter|J/m²|J/m^2
questions.e: Surface tension is force per unit length (or surface energy per unit area), so its unit is N/m (equivalently J/m²).

questions.q: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of 10 m below the surface of water? (Take density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Gauge pressure = ρgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 1 × 10^5 Pa.

questions.q: In a hydraulic lift, the small piston has area 0.01 m² and the large piston has area 1 m². If a force of 50 N is applied on the small piston, what force acts on the large piston?
questions.e: By Pascal's law F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁) = 50 × (1/0.01) = 5000 N.

questions.q: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of cross-sectional area 4 cm², which narrows to 1 cm². What is the speed of water in the narrow part?
questions.e: Equation of continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, so v₂ = (4 × 2)/1 = 8 m/s.

questions.q: If the radius of a small spherical ball falling through a viscous liquid is doubled, its terminal velocity becomes how many times the original?
questions.e: From Stokes' law, terminal velocity v = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9η), so v ∝ r². Doubling r makes v four times.

questions.q: Water (density 1000 kg/m³) flows through a horizontal pipe. Its speed increases from 1 m/s to 3 m/s at a constriction. What is the drop in pressure at the constriction?
questions.e: Bernoulli (horizontal): P₁ − P₂ = ½ρ(v₂² − v₁²) = ½ × 1000 × (9 − 1) = 4000 Pa.

questions.q: Water (surface tension 0.07 N/m, angle of contact 0°, density 1000 kg/m³) rises in a capillary tube of radius 0.1 mm. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the height of capillary rise in cm?
What is the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 1 cm if the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.03 N/m?
questions.e: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so excess pressure = 4S/r = (4 × 0.03)/0.01 = 12 Pa.

questions.q: According to the law of equipartition of energy, in thermal equilibrium each degree of freedom of a molecule has an average energy of ______ k_B T.
questions.e: Each quadratic term (degree of freedom) in the energy contributes an average of ½ k_B T per molecule.

questions.q: How many translational degrees of freedom does a molecule of a monatomic gas have?
questions.e: A monatomic molecule can move independently along x, y and z, giving 3 translational degrees of freedom.

questions.q: The number of molecules in one mole of any substance is called the ______ number.
questions.e: Avogadro's number N_A ≈ 6.02 × 10^23 per mole.

questions.q: The temperature of an ideal gas is raised from 300 K to 1200 K. By what factor does the rms speed of its molecules increase?
questions.e: v_rms = √(3k_BT/m) ∝ √T, so the factor is √(1200/300) = √4 = 2.

questions.q: What is the ratio of specific heats γ = Cp/Cv for a monatomic ideal gas? Give your answer to two decimal places.
questions.e: For a monatomic gas Cv = (3/2)R and Cp = (5/2)R, so γ = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

questions.q: The molar specific heat at constant volume of a rigid diatomic ideal gas is ______ R.
questions.e: A rigid diatomic molecule has 3 translational + 2 rotational degrees of freedom, so U = (5/2)RT per mole and Cv = (5/2)R.

questions.q: An ideal gas has density 1.2 kg/m³ at a pressure of 1.0 × 10^5 Pa. What is the rms speed of its molecules?
What is the ratio of the rms speed of hydrogen molecules (molar mass 2 g/mol) to that of oxygen molecules (molar mass 32 g/mol) at the same temperature?
questions.e: v_rms ∝ 1/√M at a given T, so v_H₂/v_O₂ = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.

questions.q: If the diameter of the gas molecules were doubled while the number density stays the same, the mean free path would become how many times its original value? Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.e: Mean free path l = 1/(√2 n π d²) ∝ 1/d², so doubling d makes l one-fourth, i.e. 0.25 times.

questions.q: A mixture contains 2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas and 1 mol of a rigid diatomic ideal gas at temperature T. Its total internal energy is x RT. What is x?
In the Geiger–Marsden alpha-particle scattering experiment, alpha particles were directed at a thin foil of ______.
questions.e: A thin gold foil (about 2.1 × 10^-7 m thick) was used; most alpha particles passed through but a few were scattered through large angles.

questions.q: What is the energy of the electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom?
questions.e: E_n = −13.6/n² eV; for n = 1, E = −13.6 eV (negative because the electron is bound).

questions.q: The series of hydrogen spectral lines that lies in the visible region is called the ______ series.
questions.e: Transitions ending on n = 2 form the Balmer series, whose first lines (Hα, Hβ, ...) lie in the visible region.

questions.q: According to Bohr's postulate, the angular momentum of the electron in a stationary orbit is an integral multiple of ______.
questions.e: Bohr's second postulate: L = nh/(2π), i.e. an integral multiple of h/2π.

questions.q: The radius of the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen is 0.53 Å. What is the radius of the n = 3 orbit?
questions.e: r_n = n² a₀, so r₃ = 9 × 0.53 Å = 4.77 Å.

questions.q: How much energy is needed to ionise a hydrogen atom whose electron is in the first excited state (n = 2)?
questions.e: E₂ = −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV, so 3.4 eV is needed to remove the electron to n = ∞.

questions.q: What is the energy of the photon emitted when the electron in a hydrogen atom jumps from n = 2 to n = 1?
Hydrogen atoms are excited to the n = 4 level. What is the maximum number of different spectral lines that can be emitted as they return to the ground state?
questions.e: Number of possible transitions = n(n − 1)/2 = 4 × 3/2 = 6.

questions.q: Using the Rydberg constant R = 1.097 × 10^7 m^-1, find the wavelength of the first line (Hα) of the Balmer series of hydrogen, to the nearest nm.
What is the ratio of the longest wavelength of the Lyman series to the longest wavelength of the Balmer series of hydrogen? Give your answer to three decimal places.
questions.e: Lyman longest: 1/λ = R(1 − 1/4) = 3R/4; Balmer longest: 1/λ = 5R/36. Ratio λ_L/λ_B = (5/36)/(3/4) = 5/27 ≈ 0.185.

questions.q: Nuclides of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called ______.
questions.e: Isotopes have the same Z (same number of protons) but different numbers of neutrons, hence different A.

questions.q: The energy equivalent of 1 atomic mass unit (1 u) is about how many MeV? Give your answer to one decimal place.
questions.e: E = mc² for 1 u = 1.6605 × 10^-27 kg gives about 931.5 MeV.

questions.q: The energy of the Sun and other stars is produced mainly by nuclear ______.
questions.e: In the Sun's core, hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium (thermonuclear fusion), releasing energy.

questions.q: Taking R₀ = 1.2 fm, what is the radius of a nucleus with mass number A = 125?
The nuclear force between nucleons is very strong but ______ range, becoming negligible beyond a few femtometres.
questions.e: Nuclear force is a short-range force, effective only up to a few fm, unlike gravitational and Coulomb forces.

questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum (about 8.75 MeV) for nuclei of which element?
questions.e: The binding energy per nucleon curve peaks near A = 56 (iron), making such nuclei the most stable.

questions.q: The mass defect of a deuteron is 0.00239 u. Taking 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c², what is its binding energy to two decimal places?
In the fission reaction ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + x n, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Mass number balance: 235 + 1 = 141 + 92 + x, so x = 3 (charge also balances: 92 = 56 + 36).

questions.q: Mass of ⁴He atom = 4.002603 u, mass of ¹H atom = 1.007825 u, mass of neutron = 1.008665 u. Taking 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c², find the binding energy per nucleon of ⁴He to two decimal places.
What is the ratio of the nuclear density of ²⁷Al to that of ¹²⁵Te?
questions.e: Since R ∝ A^(1/3), nuclear volume ∝ A and mass ∝ A, so nuclear density is independent of A; the ratio is 1.

questions.q: The SI base unit of electric current is the ______.
questions.e: The ampere is one of the seven SI base units; the volt, coulomb and ohm are derived units.

questions.q: How many base quantities are there in the SI system?
questions.e: Length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.

questions.q: A light year is a unit of ______.
questions.e: It is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 × 10^15 m.

questions.q: How many significant figures are there in 2.300 × 10^3?
questions.e: In scientific notation, all digits of 2.300 are significant, including the trailing zeros after the decimal point.

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of velocity?
questions.e: Velocity = displacement ÷ time, so its dimensions are [L] ÷ [T] = [LT^-1].

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of work (or energy)?
questions.e: Work = force × distance = [MLT^-2] × [L] = [ML^2T^-2].

questions.q: One astronomical unit (AU) is the mean distance between the Earth and the ______.
questions.e: 1 AU is about 1.496 × 10^11 m.

questions.q: Round off 2.746 to three significant figures.
questions.e: The digit dropped is 6, which is more than 5, so the preceding digit 4 is raised to 5.

questions.q: The length and breadth of a rectangle are measured with errors of 1% and 2%. What is the largest possible percentage error in its area?
questions.e: For a product, the relative errors add: 1% + 2% = 3%.

questions.q: By dimensional analysis, the period of a simple pendulum is T ∝ l^a g^b, where l is its length and g the acceleration due to gravity. What is a?
questions.e: [T] = [L]^a [LT^-2]^b gives a + b = 0 and −2b = 1, so b = −1/2 and a = 1/2.

questions.q: A quantity is calculated as P = a^3 b^2 ÷ c. The percentage errors in a, b and c are 1%, 2% and 3%.
p: (a) What is the percentage error in P?
(b) How much of this error comes from a?
questions.e: Relative error in P = 3(1%) + 2(2%) + 1(3%) = 3% + 4% + 3% = 10%; the term in a contributes 3 × 1% = 3%.

questions.q: If the velocity of an object is constant, what is its acceleration?
questions.e: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; a constant velocity does not change.

questions.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives the ______.
questions.e: Slope = change in velocity ÷ time = acceleration.

questions.q: In free fall near the Earth's surface, ignoring air resistance, an object's acceleration is about ______ m/s^2, directed downwards.
questions.e: This is the acceleration due to gravity, g.

questions.q: A car travels at 54 km/h. What is this speed in m/s?
A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s^2. What is its velocity after 3 s?
A ball is dropped from a height of 45 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.e: h = ½gt^2 gives 45 = 5t^2, so t = 3 s.

questions.q: The position of an object is x = 3t^2 m, where t is in seconds. What is its velocity at t = 2 s?
A car speeds up uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s over a distance of 100 m. What is its acceleration?
A stone is thrown vertically upwards at 30 m/s. After how many seconds does it return to the thrower's hand? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.e: It takes u ÷ g = 3 s to rise and the same time to fall back, 6 s in all.

questions.q: A car drives 40 km east in 1 h and then 40 km west back to the start in 1 h. What is its average velocity for the whole trip?
questions.e: The displacement is zero, so the average velocity is zero (the average speed is 40 km/h).

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 15 m/s from the top of a building 20 m high. (g = 10 m/s^2)
p: (a) After how long does it hit the ground?
(b) With what speed does it hit the ground?
questions.e: Taking up as positive, −20 = 15t − 5t^2 gives t^2 − 3t − 4 = 0, so t = 4 s; v = 15 − 10 × 4 = −25 m/s, a speed of 25 m/s.

questions.q: A quantity that has both magnitude and direction is called a ______ quantity.
questions.e: Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.

questions.q: Which of these is a scalar: displacement, velocity, speed or acceleration?
questions.e: Speed has only magnitude; the others also have a direction.

questions.q: At the highest point of a projectile's path, what is the vertical component of its velocity?
questions.e: The projectile stops rising for an instant; only the horizontal component remains.

questions.q: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act on a body at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
A vector of magnitude 10 units makes an angle of 60° with the x-axis. What is its x-component?
questions.e: Ax = A cos 60° = 10 × 0.5 = 5 units.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the body is directed ______.
questions.a: towards the centre|towards the center|to the centre|to the center
questions.e: This centripetal acceleration has magnitude v^2 ÷ r.

questions.q: A projectile is fired at 30 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. What is its time of flight? (g = 10 m/s^2)
A projectile is fired at 30 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. What maximum height does it reach? (g = 10 m/s^2)
A car moves round a circular track of radius 100 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
For the same launch speed, a projectile has the same horizontal range at two angles. If one angle is 30°, what is the other?
questions.e: R = u^2 sin 2θ ÷ g, and sin 60° = sin 120°, so complementary angles (θ and 90° − θ) give the same range.

questions.q: A body moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed, completing one revolution in π seconds.
questions.e: ω = 2π ÷ T = 2π ÷ π = 2 rad/s; v = ωr = 4 m/s; a = ω^2 r = 8 m/s^2.

questions.q: The product of a force and the time for which it acts is called ______.
questions.e: Impulse equals the change in momentum it produces.

questions.q: Which of Newton's laws gives the relation F = ma? Answer first, second or third.
questions.e: The second law says the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force.

questions.q: Friction always opposes the ______ motion between two surfaces in contact.
questions.e: Friction acts along the surfaces, against their relative motion (or its tendency).

questions.q: A gun of mass 5 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g at 500 m/s. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
questions.e: By conservation of momentum, 5V = 0.02 × 500 = 10, so V = 2 m/s.

questions.q: A body is in equilibrium under the action of three forces. What is the net force on it?
questions.e: In equilibrium the vector sum of all the forces is zero.

questions.q: What is the weight of a 5 kg body? (g = 10 m/s^2)
Rolling friction is generally ______ than sliding friction.
questions.e: This is why wheels and ball bearings make motion easier.

questions.q: A person of mass 60 kg stands on a weighing scale in a lift that accelerates upwards at 2 m/s^2. What does the scale read, in newtons? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.e: N − mg = ma, so N = m(g + a) = 60 × 12 = 720 N.

questions.q: The same 60 kg person is in a lift that accelerates downwards at 2 m/s^2. What does the scale read, in newtons? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.e: mg − N = ma, so N = m(g − a) = 60 × 8 = 480 N.

questions.q: A force of 10 N acts on a body for 0.5 s. What impulse does it give the body?
questions.e: Impulse = F × t = 10 × 0.5 = 5 N s.

questions.q: Blocks of 2 kg and 3 kg are placed in contact on a smooth floor. A horizontal force of 10 N pushes the 2 kg block, which pushes the 3 kg block.
p: (a) What is the acceleration of the blocks?
(b) What force does the 2 kg block exert on the 3 kg block?
questions.e: a = 10 ÷ (2 + 3) = 2 m/s^2. The 3 kg block needs F = 3 × 2 = 6 N, supplied by the 2 kg block.

questions.q: The SI unit of work and of energy is the ______.
The work-energy theorem says that the work done by the net force on a body equals the change in its ______ energy.
questions.e: W = K<sub>f</sub> − K<sub>i</sub>.

questions.q: In a perfectly elastic collision, momentum is conserved and so is the total ______.
questions.e: In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is lost.

questions.q: A force F = (3 i + 4 j) N produces a displacement d = (2 i + j) m. How much work is done?
How much work is done in lifting a 10 kg mass vertically through 2 m at constant speed? (g = 10 m/s^2)
If the momentum of a body is doubled, how many times larger does its kinetic energy become?
questions.e: K = p^2 ÷ 2m, so doubling p makes K four times larger.

questions.q: How many megajoules are there in 1 kilowatt hour?
A body of mass 1 kg has a kinetic energy of 50 J. What is its speed?
A ball is dropped from a height of 20 m. What is its speed just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 m/s^2, no air resistance)
questions.e: mgh = ½mv^2 gives v = √(2gh) = √400 = 20 m/s.

questions.q: A machine does 1500 J of work in one minute. What is its average power?
A 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s collides head-on, perfectly elastically, with an identical ball at rest.
p: (a) What is the velocity of the first ball after the collision?
(b) What is the velocity of the second ball after the collision?
questions.e: In a one-dimensional elastic collision of equal masses, the balls exchange velocities.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of torque?
questions.e: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, so it is measured in newton metres.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The rotational analogue of linear momentum is ______.
questions.e: Angular momentum L = r × p, or Iω for a rigid body.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The point at which the whole mass of a body can be considered to be concentrated is called its ______.
questions.e: For a uniform rod it is at the midpoint.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Masses of 1 kg and 3 kg are placed at x = 0 and x = 4 m. Where is their centre of mass?
questions.e: x = (1 × 0 + 3 × 4) ÷ (1 + 3) = 3 m, closer to the heavier mass.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The rate of change of angular momentum of a body equals the external ______ acting on it.
questions.e: τ = dL/dt is the rotational form of Newton's second law.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A body with moment of inertia 2 kg m^2 rotates at 5 rad/s. What is its angular momentum?

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A body with moment of inertia 4 kg m^2 rotates at 3 rad/s. What is its rotational kinetic energy?

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: For a rigid body to be in mechanical equilibrium, the net external force and the net external ______ must both be zero.
questions.e: Zero net force gives translational equilibrium; zero net torque gives rotational equilibrium.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a body depends on its mass and on how that mass is distributed about the ______.
questions.e: The same body has different moments of inertia about different axes.

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A flywheel's angular speed rises uniformly from 10 rad/s to 30 rad/s in 5 s. What is its angular acceleration?

questions.t: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A disc with moment of inertia 2 kg m^2 rotates at 10 rad/s. A constant torque brings it to rest in 4 s.
p: (a) What is its initial angular momentum?
(b) What is the size of the torque?
questions.e: L = Iω = 20 kg m^2/s, and τ = change in L ÷ time = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 N m.

questions.q: Kepler's first law says that planets move in ______ orbits with the Sun at one focus.
questions.e: This is the law of orbits.

questions.q: As we go up from the Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity ______.
questions.e: g(h) = g(1 − 2h/R) for small heights, so g falls with height.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the gravitational constant G?
questions.a: N m^2 kg^-2|N m^2/kg^2|Nm^2/kg^2|N m2 kg-2
questions.e: From F = Gm<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub>/r^2, G = Fr^2/(m<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub>), so its unit is N m^2 kg^-2.

questions.q: By Kepler's third law, the square of a planet's period is proportional to the cube of its mean distance from the Sun. What power of the distance is T^2 proportional to?
questions.e: T^2 ∝ r^3 (the law of periods).

questions.q: What is the value of g at the centre of the Earth?
questions.e: g(d) = g(1 − d/R), which is zero at d = R.

questions.q: The escape speed from a planet does not depend on the ______ of the object being launched.
questions.e: v<sub>e</sub> = √(2GM/R) contains only the planet's mass and radius.

questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of two masses is taken as ______ when they are infinitely far apart.
questions.e: With this choice, the potential energy at any finite distance is negative: −GMm/r.

questions.q: If the Earth shrank to half its radius with the same mass, the value of g at its surface would become how many times larger?
questions.e: g = GM/R^2, so halving R makes g four times larger.

questions.q: A body weighs 72 N on the Earth's surface. What does it weigh at a height equal to half the Earth's radius?
questions.e: g' = g R^2 ÷ (1.5R)^2 = 4g/9, so the weight is 72 × 4/9 = 32 N.

questions.q: For a height h much smaller than the Earth's radius, the gain in gravitational potential energy of a mass m raised through h is ______.
questions.e: For h ≪ R, g is nearly constant, so the change in potential energy is mgh.

questions.q: A planet has 4 times the mass and 2 times the radius of the Earth.
p: (a) The value of g on its surface is how many times that on the Earth?
(b) What does a body that weighs 600 N on the Earth weigh there?
questions.e: g ∝ M/R^2 = 4 ÷ 2^2 = 1, so g is the same and the body still weighs 600 N.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.a: J/(kg K)|J kg^-1 K^-1|J/kg K|J/kgK|J/(kg K^-1)
questions.e: Specific heat capacity is the heat per unit mass per unit change in temperature.

questions.q: The heat needed to change the state of unit mass of a substance, without any change in temperature, is called ______ heat.
questions.e: For water, the latent heat of fusion is 3.34 × 10^5 J/kg and of vaporisation 22.6 × 10^5 J/kg.

questions.q: In solids, heat is transferred mainly by ______.
questions.e: In conduction, heat passes from particle to particle without the particles moving from place to place.

questions.q: Sea breezes during the day are an example of heat transfer by ______.
questions.e: Land heats faster; warm air over it rises and cooler air moves in from the sea.

questions.q: Water has its maximum density at ______.
questions.e: This anomalous expansion lets lakes freeze from the top while water below stays at about 4 °C.

questions.q: Convert 212 °F into degrees Celsius.
2000 J of heat raises the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 5 K. What is its specific heat capacity?
A rod 2 m long with coefficient of linear expansion 1 × 10^-5 per K is heated through 100 K. By how many millimetres does it lengthen?
How much heat is needed to melt 2 kg of ice at 0 °C? (Latent heat of fusion = 3.34 × 10^5 J/kg)
By Newton's law of cooling, the rate at which a body cools is proportional to the ______ between the body and its surroundings.
questions.e: −dQ/dt = k(T − T<sub>s</sub>) for small temperature differences.

questions.q: For an isotropic solid, the coefficient of volume expansion is about how many times its coefficient of linear expansion?
questions.e: α<sub>V</sub> = 3α<sub>l</sub>.

questions.q: 100 g of water at 80 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 20 °C. No heat is lost. (Specific heat of water = 4200 J/(kg K))
p: (b) How much heat does the hot water lose?
questions.e: Equal masses of water settle at the average, 50 °C. Heat lost = 0.1 × 4200 × 30 = 12 600 J.

questions.q: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other. Which law of thermodynamics is this?
questions.e: The zeroth law is the basis of temperature measurement.

questions.q: A process in which no heat enters or leaves the system is called ______.
questions.e: It happens in a thermally insulated container or when the process is very fast.

questions.q: A process that takes place at constant pressure is called ______.
questions.e: Isochoric means constant volume; isothermal means constant temperature.

questions.q: In an isochoric (constant-volume) process, how much work is done by the gas?
questions.e: W = PΔV, and ΔV = 0.

questions.q: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 1 × 10^5 Pa from 0.001 m^3 to 0.003 m^3. How much work does it do?
In a cyclic process, what is the change in the internal energy of the system?
questions.e: The system returns to its initial state, so its internal energy is the same.

questions.q: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its ______.
questions.e: There are no intermolecular forces in an ideal gas, so its internal energy is purely kinetic.

questions.q: 100 J of heat is supplied to a gas kept at constant volume. By how much does its internal energy increase?
questions.e: No work is done at constant volume, so ΔU = Q = 100 J.

questions.q: In an isothermal process of an ideal gas, what is the change in internal energy?
questions.e: The temperature is constant, so the internal energy does not change and Q = W.

questions.q: What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine working between 400 K and 300 K?
For one mole of an ideal gas, C<sub>p</sub> − C<sub>v</sub> equals ______.
questions.e: This is Mayer's relation; R is the universal gas constant.

questions.q: A gas absorbs 800 J of heat and its internal energy increases by 500 J.
p: (a) How much work does the gas do?
(b) If the same 800 J were given at constant volume, by how much would the internal energy increase?
questions.e: By the first law, W = Q − ΔU = 800 − 500 = 300 J. At constant volume W = 0, so ΔU = Q = 800 J.

questions.q: The time taken to complete one oscillation is called the ______.
questions.e: Period T = 1 ÷ frequency.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the speed of the particle is greatest at the ______ position.
questions.e: At the mean position all the energy is kinetic.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the particle is greatest at the ______ positions.
questions.e: a = −ω^2 x, which is largest where the displacement is largest.

questions.q: A particle in SHM has an amplitude of 4 cm. What distance does it travel in one complete oscillation?
questions.e: In one oscillation it goes from the mean position to one extreme, back, to the other extreme and back: 4A = 16 cm (its displacement is zero).

questions.q: A particle in SHM has a frequency of 5 Hz. What is its time period?
If the length of a simple pendulum is made 4 times larger, its time period becomes how many times larger?
questions.e: T = 2π√(l/g), so T ∝ √l.

questions.q: The period of a mass on a spring is T = 2π√(m/k). If the mass is made 4 times larger, the period becomes how many times larger?
questions.e: T ∝ √m.

questions.q: For a given oscillator, the total energy in simple harmonic motion is proportional to the square of its ______.
questions.e: E = ½kA^2, which stays constant during the motion.

questions.q: A particle in SHM has an amplitude of 0.1 m and an angular frequency of 10 rad/s. What is its maximum acceleration?
A spring stretches by 0.1 m when a 1 kg mass hangs from it. What is its spring constant? (g = 10 m/s^2)
A simple pendulum has a period of 2 s on the Earth. What would its period be on a planet where g is one-fourth of the Earth's?
questions.e: T ∝ 1/√g, so a quarter of g doubles the period.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle is x = 0.05 cos(4πt) m, where t is in seconds.
questions.e: Compare with x = A cos(ωt): A = 0.05 m and ω = 4π rad/s, so ν = ω ÷ 2π = 2 Hz and T = 0.5 s.

questions.q: Waves in which the particles of the medium vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel of the wave are called ______ waves.
questions.e: Waves on a stretched string are transverse.

questions.q: The distance between two consecutive crests of a wave is called its ______.
questions.e: Wavelength is also the distance between two consecutive troughs.

questions.q: In a stationary wave, the points where the displacement is always zero are called ______.
questions.e: Points of maximum displacement are antinodes.

questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave on a string is v = √(T/μ). If the tension is made 4 times larger, the speed becomes how many times larger?
questions.e: v ∝ √T.

questions.q: When two sound waves of slightly different frequencies are heard together, the loudness rises and falls periodically. These are called ______.
questions.e: The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies.

questions.q: Two tuning forks of 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. How many beats are heard per second?
questions.e: Beat frequency = 260 − 256 = 4 Hz.

questions.q: The distance between two consecutive nodes in a stationary wave is what fraction of the wavelength?
questions.e: Consecutive nodes are λ/2 apart; a node and the next antinode are λ/4 apart.

questions.q: A wave travels at 330 m/s with a wavelength of 1.5 m. What is its frequency?
A string 1 m long is fixed at both ends. What is the wavelength of its fundamental mode of vibration?
questions.e: In the fundamental mode, L = λ/2, so λ = 2L = 2 m.

questions.q: A pipe open at both ends is 0.5 m long. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.e: For an open pipe, ν = v ÷ 2L = 340 ÷ 1 = 340 Hz.

questions.q: Newton's formula for the speed of sound in air gave too low a value. Who corrected it by treating the process as adiabatic?
questions.e: Laplace used v = √(γP/ρ), which agrees with experiment.

questions.q: The speed of sound in a gas ______ as its temperature rises.
questions.e: v ∝ √T for a gas, where T is the absolute temperature.

questions.q: A string 0.5 m long, fixed at both ends, carries waves at 100 m/s.
p: (b) What is the frequency of its second harmonic?
questions.e: ν<sub>1</sub> = v ÷ 2L = 100 ÷ 1 = 100 Hz; the second harmonic is 2ν<sub>1</sub> = 200 Hz.

questions.q: The property of a body by which it regains its original size and shape when the deforming force is removed is called ______.
questions.e: A body that does not regain its shape is called plastic.

questions.q: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal ______.
questions.e: Y = (F/A) ÷ (ΔL/L).

questions.q: The ratio of shearing stress to shearing strain is called the ______ modulus.
questions.e: The shear modulus is also called the modulus of rigidity, G.

questions.q: A material that breaks soon after its elastic limit is crossed is called ______.
questions.e: Glass and cast iron are brittle; ductile materials such as copper stretch a lot before breaking.

questions.q: Within the elastic limit, a wire stretches by 2 mm under a load of 40 N. How much does it stretch under 60 N?
questions.e: Extension is proportional to load (Hooke's law): 2 × 60/40 = 3 mm.

questions.q: A steel rod 1 m long with a cross-sectional area of 1 cm^2 is pulled by a force of 2 × 10^4 N. (Young's modulus of steel = 2 × 10^11 Pa)
p: (a) What is the stress in the rod, in units of 10^8 Pa?
(b) By how many millimetres does the rod stretch?
questions.e: Stress = 2 × 10^4 ÷ 10^-4 = 2 × 10^8 Pa. Strain = stress ÷ Y = 10^-3, so the extension is 10^-3 × 1 m = 1 mm.

questions.q: By Pascal's law, a pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted ______ to every part of the fluid.
questions.e: This is the principle of the hydraulic lift and hydraulic brakes.

questions.q: The property of a fluid that opposes relative motion between its layers is called ______.
questions.e: Honey is more viscous than water.

questions.q: Bernoulli's principle for a flowing fluid is based on the conservation of ______.
questions.e: Pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy per unit volume add up to a constant along a streamline.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity?
questions.a: Pa s|pascal second|N s m^-2|N s/m^2|poiseuille
questions.e: η = (F/A) ÷ (velocity gradient), giving N s m^-2, which is the same as Pa s.

questions.q: At sea level, the atmosphere supports a column of mercury in a barometer about ______ high.
questions.e: This is 1 atm, about 1.013 × 10^5 Pa.

questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. At point A the area is 0.02 m^2 and the speed is 1 m/s; at point B the area is 0.01 m^2. (Density of water = 1000 kg/m^3)
p: (a) What is the speed of the water at B?
(b) How much greater is the pressure at A than at B?
questions.e: Continuity: 0.02 × 1 = 0.01 × v, so v = 2 m/s. Bernoulli: P<sub>A</sub> − P<sub>B</sub> = ½ × 1000 × (2^2 − 1^2) = 1500 Pa.

questions.q: The ideal gas equation for n moles of gas is PV = ______.
questions.e: R is the universal gas constant, 8.314 J/(mol K).

questions.q: By Boyle's law, at constant temperature the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its ______.
questions.e: PV = constant at constant temperature.

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of a gas molecule is directly proportional to the ______ temperature.
questions.e: Average kinetic energy = (3/2)k<sub>B</sub>T, with T in kelvin.

questions.q: At constant pressure, a gas at 300 K is heated until its volume doubles. What is its final temperature?
questions.e: By Charles's law V ∝ T, so doubling V doubles T.

questions.q: How many degrees of freedom (translational plus rotational) does a rigid diatomic molecule have?
questions.e: Three translational and two rotational degrees of freedom.

questions.q: A gas in a closed rigid container is at 27 °C and 2 atm. It is heated to 327 °C.
p: (a) What is the final temperature in kelvin?
questions.e: 327 + 273 = 600 K. At constant volume P ∝ T, so P = 2 × 600/300 = 4 atm.
